title: The Visitation: Second Joyful Mystery
summary: Pray the Second Joyful Mystery page by page: the story of the Visitation, the Gospel, the decade prayers, and a quiet reflection.
coverAlt: Ghirlandaio's painting of the Visitation: Mary and Elizabeth embrace with joy.

pages.title: The Visitation
pages.body: Mary went quickly through the hill country to help her cousin Elizabeth, who was expecting a baby. When Mary greeted her, the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy, because Mary was carrying Jesus. As we pray this decade, we think of Mary bringing Jesus to others, and we ask to carry his love to the people we meet.
pages.imageAlt: Ghirlandaio's painting of the Visitation: Mary and Elizabeth embrace with joy.

evidence.claim: Original child-friendly meditation on the mystery; the mystery and its traditional day follow the standard Rosary order.

pages.title: From the Gospel
pages.body:
God's Word tells us this mystery. From the Gospel according to Luke, chapter 1 (Douay-Rheims Bible):

“And Mary rising up in those days, went into the hill country with haste into a city of Juda. And she entered into the house of Zachary, and saluted Elizabeth. And it came to pass, that when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost: And she cried out with a loud voice, and said: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.”

(Luke 1:39-45)

evidence.claim: Scripture quotation reproduced word for word from the Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition (public domain); verse numbers omitted for reading aloud and ellipses mark skipped verses.

pages.title: Praying the Decade
pages.body:
We announce the mystery: The Visitation, the Second Joyful Mystery. Then we pray one decade of the Rosary, holding this scene in our hearts.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (We pray the Hail Mary ten times, once for each bead of the decade.)

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell; lead all souls to Heaven, especially those in most need of Thy mercy.

evidence.claim: The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers use the standard formulas printed across this site.

pages.title: The Fruit of This Mystery: Charity and joyful service
pages.body:
This mystery grows the fruit of charity and joyful service. Mary's first thought after the angel's visit was someone else. Who near you could use a visit, a call, or a helping hand this week?

Let us pray: Lord Jesus, teach us to carry your love to others, as Mary carried you. Amen. Our Lady of the Rosary, pray for us.

evidence.claim: Original reflection and closing prayer; the fruit of the mystery follows the traditional list used across this site.
